title: Measure scientific non-inferiority of CPU, CUDA and hybrid motion correction

latest_comments.body:
## Outcome reversed on review: Stage B verdicts withdrawn to INCONCLUSIVE

Following the Codex and Copilot reviews of [PR #65](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/65) at `ef5935e`, and a second review round on the fixes themselves, **the non-inferiority conclusion I posted on 2026-09-25 does not stand.** Full disposition in the [PR thread](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/65); the substance for this issue:

### What was wrong

The validity precondition claimed the endpoint could resolve its harm margin because `ctrl_noise_f005` sat 5.8 SE from `rho = 1.0`. It did not: that control measured `rho = 0.9666` and **passed** the 0.95 margin, so it never exercised the decision the endpoint makes. I added four margin-calibrated controls and a criterion **S1** — "no control at or beyond the margin may earn a PASS" — and reported it demonstrated at `rho = 0.94914`.

**S1 is vacuous.** A one-sided lower bound satisfies `lower95 <= rho` by construction, so any control classified harmful by its measured `rho` can never pass; the criterion could not fail. It has content only for a margin-designed control whose measured `rho` lands *above* the margin, and none did.

That leaves only positive rejection, demonstrated at `rho = 0.9146` — an 8.5% effective-data loss, not the 5% margin. **Sensitivity at the prespecified harm margin is unproven**, so every Stage B verdict for `default` and `allfftw` is withdrawn from PASS to INCONCLUSIVE under [Amendment 2](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/feat/issue-61-scientific-noninferiority/docs/issue61_noninferiority/PROTOCOL.md#10-amendments).

### Revised answer to this issue's pass criteria

| Stage | Endpoint | `default` | `allfftw` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | CTF max resolution / defocus / FoM | PASS* | PASS* |
| **B** | **effective-data fraction `rho`** | **INCONCLUSIVE** | **INCONCLUSIVE** |
| B | `d143`, auto-B | INCONCLUSIVE | INCONCLUSIVE |
| C | `d143`, auto-B after independent refinement | PASS** | PASS** / INCONCLUSIVE |

\* Stage A's own controls show it cannot detect a 5% loss, and CTF max resolution does not move even under a 20% one.
\*\* Stage C has **no positive control at all**, and its within-arm seed spread (0.062 Å) exceeds every between-arm difference it measured.

**No prespecified endpoint supports a non-inferiority conclusion for either backend.** That is a statement about the evidence, not about the backends.

### What does still stand

- Both accelerated arms are **measurably indistinguishable from CPU at the precision achieved**: observed effective-data loss 4.1e-5 and 1.9e-5, bounds 162x and 610x inside the allowed loss, under a matched design now verified field-by-field (18 named fields, 6 arms, 144 stacks, one shared metadata digest).
- The endpoint **does** detect an 8.5% loss and tracks four designed degradation levels quantitatively — it is not inert.
- The specificity result is unaffected and remains the sharpest thing here: a deterministic envelope removing **81% of 3-2 Å power** leaves FSC and resolution **unchanged**. Image difference does not imply signal loss. This still converges with #60's independent finding that the 0.001 relative-RMSE limit is a near-binary "not bit-identical" detector.
- No measurement changed. Every endpoint value, bound and all 72 pixel digests reproduce exactly. **No margin, threshold or gate was relaxed** — both amendments are tightenings, and the second removes a conclusion.

### The one experiment that would resolve it

≥20 independent noise realisations of a margin-designed control (`f = 0.062`), full jackknife each, counting how many wrongly yield `lower95 >= 0.95`; plus a replicate set at the real arms' precision scale (`SE ~ 1.6e-4` vs `~8e-3`). ≈920 reconstructions + 460 post-processing runs, ~50 min of exclusive `cpu64` lock. **Not run** — it is a design-validation study rather than a review fix, so I have left the decision to you.

Compute: `cpu64` cores 32-63 / NUMA node 1, ≤12 concurrent, behind the issue-96 validation lock, `ctffind` untouched, no GPU and no SCARF allocation. Read-only passes on `4GPUs` used cores 120-123, outside both reservations. Not merging or closing.

Data point for this study, from #171 (experimental `--fft_size_policy fast`: 7-smooth padded FFTs, hidden and off by default).

**Speed:** 96 movies 25.88 → 22.64 s (−13.4%), 24 movies 7.19 → 6.13 s (−12.6%). Products differ, so these are speed-only verdicts.

**Validation against the CPU reference, existing gates unchanged:** it fails.

| what is padded | movies passing | worst image RMSE (gate 0.02) | max local trajectory change |
|---|---|---|---|
| nothing (default) | 24/24 | 0.009 | 0.065 px |
| frames and patches | 0/24 | 0.049 | 0.72 px |
| frames only | 0/24 | 0.046 | 0.74 px |
| patches only | 3/24 | 0.038 | 0.36 px |

**Where the error comes from:**
- **Frame padding** replaces the periodic wrap at the image edges with mean fill: 58% of the squared error is in the outer 8 px.
- **Patch padding** changes the fitted local motion model by up to 0.36 px.
- Dose weighting is not the cause.

**The current gates are also too coarse to validate a mode like this.** A dose-weight grid wrong by 1% of each axis falls below their resolution. Any future non-identical speed mode needs finer, calibrated gates first (#60).
